title: Security Effect is the Pit Boss, not the nightclub bouncer
summary: Security Effect (Bouncer) is an evidence-producing business-security reasoning domain. It describes what is observed, what concern applies to one proposed action, uncertainty/counterevidence, and proportionate constraints. It is not a firewall, moral judge, generic customer risk score, or method-authority service.
invariants: Risk and concern attach to the proposed action and current evidence, not to character or a permanent score on a person.
A suspicious session may retain low-consequence abilities while high-consequence actions are held or reviewed.
Security Effect produces business understanding; downstream authority and enforcement remain separate.
No runtime LLM judgement is part of the operative decision path.

provenance.claim: README defines Bouncer as action-scoped deterministic security reasoning and separates it from perimeter/enforcement roles.
Architecture defines Security Effect as an action-scoped business-security reasoning domain.
